open_points.subject: viewer access management authority
open_points.text: “created by an operator” and “re-issuable by an operator”; “manage client viewers, access links, and project grants”; but R0-14 says these actions “all require the access-management capability, which only administrators hold”
open_points.question: Can an operator create or revoke viewers, re-issue access links, or manage viewer grants, or are all of those actions administrator-only?
options: Operator and administrator may perform them
Administrator only
open_points.default_guess: Administrator only, following R0-14.

witness.initial: An operator is assigned to project P and a client needs access.
events: The operator attempts to create a ClientViewer and issue an access link.
outcomes: The operation succeeds because the Principals and Operator management passages authorize an operator.
The operation is denied because R0-14 reserves access management to administrators.

open_points.subject: service-principal authorization
open_points.text: “Every project-scoped operation checks together: valid active session” but “Producer operations authenticate with the bearer credential of R0-09”
open_points.question: Does a service-principal bearer credential itself satisfy project-scoped authentication, or must a ServicePrincipal also have a session?
options: Bearer authentication replaces the session check for service principals
Every service principal also has a managed session
open_points.default_guess: Bearer authentication replaces the session check for service principals.

witness.initial: An active producer has a valid bearer credential and project scope but no session.
events: The producer imports a snapshot for an allowed project.
outcomes: The import succeeds under R0-09 and R0-15.
The import fails the common rule because there is no active session.

open_points.subject: ClientViewer revocation state
open_points.text: “revoking the viewer or its access credential closes all of that client's projects”
open_points.question: What concrete persisted state constitutes a revoked viewer, how does it differ from credential revocation, and can the viewer later be restored without creating a new identity?
options: ClientViewer has an active/revoked lifecycle independent of credentials
‘Revoke viewer’ means revoke every credential and grant
Viewer revocation permanently retires the identity
open_points.default_guess: Give ClientViewer an independent active/revoked status and invalidate its sessions and credentials on revocation.

witness.initial: Viewer V has two grants, one credential, and an active session.
events: An administrator revokes V.
Later an administrator issues a new credential for V.
outcomes: V can be restored and regain the still-existing grants.
V is permanently retired, so re-issuance is refused or requires a new viewer.

open_points.subject: global producer scope
open_points.text: “a global producer exists only through an explicitly granted capability” while the closed capability set names only `portal.estimate_snapshot.import` and `portal.estimate_snapshot.read_import_result`
open_points.question: What named authorization fact grants global project scope, and how is it represented separately from the two import capabilities?
options: A third named global capability
A producer-scope record denoting all projects
An administrative-area scope that happens to cover every project
open_points.default_guess: Represent global reach as an explicit producer-scope fact, not as an unnamed capability.

witness.initial: A producer has `portal.estimate_snapshot.import` but no project list.
events: It imports for a newly created Registry project.
outcomes: The import succeeds because the import capability is treated as the global grant.
The import fails because no separately represented global scope exists.

open_points.subject: manual budget mutation and versioning
open_points.text: “An authorized operator maintains ordered client-facing Budget Sections” and “manual sections are never rewritten in place”
open_points.question: How does an operator edit a manual budget without rewriting its sections: does every edit create a new immutable budget version, or are some fields mutable?
options: Every manual edit creates and activates a new version
Manual sections are mutable until transition to an imported source
Section records are replaced while stable section identities persist
open_points.default_guess: Create a new manual budget version for each committed edit while preserving stable section identities.

witness.initial: Project P has an active manual section S with planned work of €10,000.
events: An operator changes S to €12,000.
outcomes: The existing section is updated in place.
A new manual budget version and new section record are created and activated.
witness.observer: The viewer, auditor, and later domain implementer

open_points.subject: active manual budget identity
open_points.text: “at most one budget version is active per project at any time” but manual budgets are described only as “manual budgets with ordered budget sections”
open_points.question: Are manual budgets versioned members of the same activation model as imported snapshots, and may a project have no active budget version?
options: Manual and imported budgets are both versions in one activation model
Only snapshots are versioned; manual budget is a separate mutable source
Every project must always have exactly one active budget
Zero or one active budget is allowed
open_points.default_guess: Use one version/activation model for both sources and allow no active budget before initial setup.

witness.initial: A new project has no budget; an operator creates a manual budget and later imports a snapshot.
events: The manual budget is first exposed to the viewer.
The snapshot is activated.
outcomes: Both are versions and activation moves from the manual version to the snapshot version.
The manual budget is not an active version, so snapshot activation coexists with it under separate rules.

open_points.subject: activation with unmapped expenses
open_points.text: “existing allocations require explicit mapping to the sections of the newly activated version” and “unmapped expenses stay visible and must be resolved by an operator”
open_points.question: May activation complete while allocations remain unmapped, or must all required mappings be resolved before activation succeeds?
options: Activation is rejected until every allocation is mapped
Activation succeeds with an explicit unmapped state
Only affected allocations are excluded from totals until resolved
open_points.default_guess: Allow activation with an explicit unmapped state, because the text says unmapped expenses stay visible afterward.

witness.initial: The active budget has section A and an included expense allocated to A; a candidate snapshot has no corresponding stable section.
events: An operator attempts to activate the snapshot without choosing a target section.
outcomes: Activation fails until the operator maps the expense.
Activation succeeds and the expense remains visibly unmapped for later resolution.

open_points.subject: automatic section correspondence
open_points.text: “matching stable section identifiers may link automatically”
open_points.question: Which identifiers must match, who initiates the automatic link, and is the link a persisted mapping decision that can be reviewed or overridden?
options: Exact equality of a shared canonical section ID creates a persisted mapping automatically
A staff action proposes mappings for review
Automatic linking is optional implementation behavior
open_points.default_guess: Require exact equality of an explicitly shared stable identifier and persist the resulting mapping decision.

witness.initial: An old manual section has ID `A`; a new snapshot section has `source_section_id=A` but a different source code and name.
events: The new version is activated.
outcomes: The allocation is linked automatically because `A` matches.
No automatic link is made because manual IDs and source IDs are different namespaces.

open_points.subject: Other expenses allocation target
open_points.text: “`Other expenses` persists independently of budget versions” but Persistent data names no record, identity, ownership, or lifecycle for it
open_points.question: Is `Other expenses` a singleton project-owned allocation target, a real section, or a derived category, and what stable identifier is used in allocations?
options: One permanent project-owned special allocation target
A section in every budget version connected by mapping
A derived category represented by a null section reference
open_points.default_guess: Use one permanent project-owned special allocation target with a stable reserved identity.

witness.initial: An expense is allocated to Other expenses while manual budget M is active.
events: Snapshot S is activated.
The expense is read afterward.
outcomes: Its allocation still targets a permanent project-level entity.
Its allocation is represented as null or recreated against the new version, producing different persistence and query behavior.

open_points.subject: expense replay conflict
open_points.text: “One recognized document creates at most one Expense with one Document; replay is idempotent”
open_points.question: What happens when the same `recognized_document_id` is submitted again with different confirmed content, project, total, or allocation?
options: Reject as an integrity conflict
Return the original Expense regardless of differences
Treat mutable operator allocation fields as an update while preserving recognized content
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing result only for an equivalent request and reject materially different replay as an integrity conflict.

witness.initial: Recognized document R created expense E in project P for €100.
events: A staff member submits R again for project Q or with a total of €120.
outcomes: The service idempotently returns E.
The service rejects the replay as conflicting content or ownership.

open_points.subject: expense correction action
open_points.text: “an operator can: correct, include, or exclude an expense”
open_points.question: Which expense fields may be corrected, which provenance fields are immutable, and what observable failure occurs for forbidden corrections?
options: Only a closed set of client-facing normalized fields is editable
All fields except identity and project are editable
Correction creates a replacement/version rather than mutating the Expense
open_points.default_guess: Permit a closed set of normalized business-field corrections while keeping identity, project, OCR provenance, and source document reference immutable.

witness.initial: Expense E was created from confirmed OCR content in project P.
events: An operator attempts to change E's total, source reference, or project.
outcomes: All requested changes are accepted as expense corrections.
Only business fields are changed; provenance/project changes are rejected.

open_points.subject: work progress across budget versions
open_points.text: “update manual work progress per section” while source transitions specify allocation mapping but do not say what happens to work progress
open_points.question: When the active budget version changes, is section progress mapped, reset, retained against the old version, or made unavailable until entered again?
options: Map progress through the same section mappings
Reset progress for the new version
Keep version-specific progress and expose only the active version's values
Block activation until progress is explicitly migrated
open_points.default_guess: Keep progress version-specific and explicitly map it when stable section correspondence exists.

witness.initial: Manual section A is 50% complete with €10,000 planned work.
events: A snapshot with corresponding section B and €12,000 planned work is activated.
outcomes: B becomes 50% complete and completed work becomes €6,000.
B starts with unavailable or 0% progress while A's historical progress remains attached to the old version.

open_points.subject: payment replay conflict
open_points.text: “register work payments (idempotent by stable payment identity)”
open_points.question: What happens when the same payment identity is replayed with a different amount, date, project, or payer information?
options: Reject differing content as an integrity conflict
Return the existing payment and ignore differences
Update the existing payment
open_points.default_guess: Idempotently return an equivalent payment and reject differing content as an integrity conflict.

witness.initial: Payment X for €1,000 exists in project P.
events: An operator submits X again for €1,500.
outcomes: The existing €1,000 payment is returned without error.
The request is rejected as a conflicting replay.

open_points.subject: unavailable client data
open_points.text: “Unavailable data is shown explicitly, never fabricated or replaced by silent zeros”
open_points.question: How does the JSON API represent unavailable values and distinguish unavailable, not applicable, not yet entered, and an external dependency failure?
options: Null plus a closed reason code
Omitted field plus status metadata
A resource-level error response
One undifferentiated unavailable marker
open_points.default_guess: Return null with a closed machine-readable availability reason.

witness.initial: A project has no planned work cost and Registry context is temporarily unavailable.
events: A viewer requests the project view.
outcomes: The response succeeds with explicit field-level unavailable reason codes.
The request fails as a whole or returns null/omitted fields without distinguishing the causes.

open_points.subject: derived-money rounding order
open_points.text: “Money uses decimal semantics with explicit currency and domain-defined rounding”; R0-05 says “rounded half up to two places” but does not define when intermediate and aggregate values are rounded
open_points.question: For completed-work value, weighted progress, allocations, and totals, are values rounded per record/section before summing or only after the final calculation?
options: Round each section or allocation, then sum
Sum exact decimal intermediates, then round the final value
Define a separate rounding stage for each derived value
open_points.default_guess: Define a separate deterministic rounding stage for each formula; absent that, retain exact decimals through aggregation and round the final monetary result.

witness.initial: Two sections each have planned work €0.05 at 50% completion.
events: The portal computes total completed work.
outcomes: Each €0.025 rounds to €0.03 and the total is €0.06.
The exact sum €0.05 is rounded once and the total is €0.05.

open_points.subject: significant audit actions
open_points.text: “Every significant action records actor provenance”
open_points.question: What is the closed definition of a significant action, especially for successful reads, failed authorization, login attempts, challenge requests, session restoration/end, health checks, and local administrative operations?
options: Audit every authenticated business command and every security-relevant success/failure
Audit only the actions explicitly enumerated
Define separate closed audit-event sets for business and security actions
open_points.default_guess: Define closed business and security audit-event sets, including failed security operations but excluding health checks and ordinary reads.

witness.initial: A user repeatedly fails login and another viewer downloads a protected document.
events: The failed logins occur.
The authorized download succeeds.
outcomes: Both are audit records because they are security-significant.
Neither is recorded because neither appears in the enumerated examples.

open_points.subject: Registry dependency failures
open_points.text: “server-side validation before linked writes” and “typed failure translation” without naming the failure types or behavior when Registry is unavailable
open_points.question: What observable portal outcomes distinguish nonexistent, archived, forbidden, malformed, timed-out, and unavailable Registry responses for reads and writes?
options: A closed mapping to portal error codes
Fail all project operations closed with one indistinguishable dependency error
Allow cached reads but reject writes during Registry failure
open_points.default_guess: Fail writes closed and define a closed mapping of Registry lifecycle/not-found failures separately from transient dependency failure.

witness.initial: Project P was active at the last successful check, but Registry is now unreachable.
events: An operator submits an expense for P.
A viewer reads P.
outcomes: Both operations fail because current Registry validation is required.
The write fails but the read succeeds from portal-owned data or cached context.

open_points.subject: email delivery failure
open_points.text: “The gateway only delivers messages” and “delivery success or failure never counts as address confirmation”
open_points.question: What does the portal do and return when challenge or security-notification delivery fails, and are retries automatic, staff-triggered, or absent?
options: Persist the challenge and return a generic accepted result while recording delivery failure
Revoke the newly created challenge and return a delivery error
Retry according to a defined policy
Leave retry/manual reissue to a later explicit action
open_points.default_guess: Persist the challenge and delivery record, return a non-enumerating accepted response where required, and expose a controlled reissue action rather than treating delivery as confirmation.

witness.initial: An administrator issues email verification for a pending staff account.
events: The portal creates the challenge.
The email gateway reports delivery failure.
outcomes: The challenge remains valid and can be delivered by retry or reissue.
The challenge is revoked or the whole operation fails atomically.

open_points.subject: PresuPro transport binding
open_points.text: “Concrete transport between PresuPro and the portal … Decided by R0-09: a bearer header” but Open questions says “Still open … the PresuPro transport binding”
open_points.question: Is bearer-header authentication settled for PresuPro, or is its transport binding still an open later-state decision?
options: Settled: producer requests use only a bearer header
Still open among bearer, signed request, mTLS, or gateway
open_points.default_guess: Settled as bearer-only, following R0-09.

witness.initial: An implementer is defining the producer HTTP contract.
events: They read R0-09 and the Open questions list.
outcomes: They reject mTLS-only or signed-request authentication because bearer-only is decided.
They choose mTLS or signed requests because the binding is explicitly still open.

open_points.subject: bootstrap command outcomes
open_points.text: “Its outcome is a closed set of exit codes that deployment scripts may branch on”
open_points.question: What are the complete exit codes and their meanings, including success, existing staff account, invalid input, configuration failure, and persistence failure?
options: Enumerate distinct stable exit codes for each actionable outcome
Use success plus one generic failure code
Use success, refused-because-staff-exists, invalid-input, and internal/configuration failure
open_points.default_guess: Define stable codes for success, precondition refusal, invalid input, configuration error, and persistence/internal failure.

witness.initial: A deployment script invokes bootstrap against a database that already contains a staff account.
events: The command refuses creation and exits.
outcomes: It returns a dedicated ‘staff already exists’ code that the script treats as an expected refusal.
It returns the same generic failure used for malformed input or database failure.
witness.observer: The host operator and deployment script

open_points.subject: runtime configuration contract
open_points.text: “configured only by environment variables, which it validates when it starts”
open_points.question: What are the required environment-variable names, accepted formats and bounds, and the observable startup failure for missing, invalid, wildcard, or mutually inconsistent values?
options: A closed configuration schema with stable startup error categories
Implementation-defined environment names and validation messages
One generic startup refusal for every invalid configuration
open_points.default_guess: Define a closed environment-variable schema and stable non-secret startup error categories.

witness.initial: A deployment supplies a wildcard trusted host and an invalid `binary_max_read_bytes`.
events: The service starts and validates configuration.
outcomes: Startup refuses with distinct actionable configuration errors.
Startup refuses generically or accepts one value because validation details are implementation-defined.

open_points.subject: readiness semantics
open_points.text: “The service answers an unauthenticated liveness and readiness check”
open_points.question: Which conditions make liveness and readiness succeed or fail, and what stable status/body does each check return?
options: Liveness means process loop is responsive; readiness checks validated configuration, database, binary root, and required dependencies
Both checks always report process availability
Readiness checks only local persistence and not external systems
open_points.default_guess: Make liveness process-local and readiness require valid configuration plus usable SQLite and binary storage, with stable minimal status responses.

witness.initial: The process is running, but its SQLite database cannot be opened.
events: A monitor requests liveness.
The monitor requests readiness.
outcomes: Liveness succeeds and readiness fails.
Both succeed because the HTTP process can answer.

open_points.subject: binary media allowlists
open_points.text: “its media type is recognized from the content and must be on a closed list per object kind”
open_points.question: What exact media types are allowed for ExpenseDocument and ProgressPhoto, and what content-recognition authority determines them?
options: Enumerated MIME allowlists plus a named content-sniffing rule/library contract
One shared allowlist for both kinds
Implementation-defined allowlists
open_points.default_guess: Define separate enumerated MIME allowlists and determine type from byte signatures, not extensions or stored metadata.

witness.initial: An authorized ExpenseDocument contains valid TIFF bytes.
events: The viewer requests the document.
outcomes: The download succeeds because TIFF is on the document allowlist.
The request receives the indistinguishable protected-binary failure because TIFF is not allowed.

open_points.subject: protected-binary failure response
open_points.text: “An unknown, cross-project, hidden, oversize or unlisted read is answered the same way”
open_points.question: What exact HTTP status, headers, and body constitute the common indistinguishable failure, and does storage absence or read failure use that same response?
options: A fixed not-found response for every concealed condition, including missing stored bytes
A fixed forbidden response
A generic binary-unavailable response, with operational storage failures distinguished only internally
open_points.default_guess: Use one fixed not-found response for all caller-concealed cases, while logging internal storage failures without exposing them.

witness.initial: Viewer V may access project P.
events: V requests a hidden photo.
V requests a visible photo whose `file_ref` has no stored bytes.
outcomes: Both requests return exactly the same fixed response.
The hidden photo is concealed as not found, while missing storage produces a server error.

open_points.subject: prepared progress-photo facts
open_points.text: “prepared photo facts” and “a progress photo is published the same way”
open_points.question: What concrete fields constitute prepared photo facts, which fields come from the authenticated staff member versus intake, and what validation or failure outcomes apply?
options: A closed versioned photo-publication input contract
Only `file_ref` plus operator-provided caption, section, visibility, and project
An implementation-defined structure delegated to the future intake hand-over
open_points.default_guess: Define a closed versioned input containing stable intake identity, file reference, provenance and capture facts, with project, caption, section and visibility supplied authoritatively by staff.

witness.initial: A binary has been placed with a file reference and Telegram metadata containing a project and caption.
events: An authenticated operator publishes it with a different project and caption.
outcomes: Operator-supplied project and caption are authoritative and intake values are provenance only.
The prepared facts control some or all of those values, so the request is rejected or published differently.

open_points.subject: sole-administrator recovery
open_points.text: “Recovery of the sole administrator stays a deployment-level operation (R0-07)” although R0-07 defines only first-administrator creation and refuses once any staff account exists
open_points.question: What deployment-level action recovers a sole existing administrator, what authority and inputs does it require, and what are its output, audit, and failure semantics?
options: A separate local recovery command
An extension of the bootstrap command with a distinct recovery mode
No recovery operation until an operator intervenes directly in storage
open_points.default_guess: Define a separate local recovery command with explicit proof-of-host authority, secure interactive inputs, audit behavior, and closed exit codes.

witness.initial: The only administrator account exists but its login email and password are inaccessible.
events: The host operator invokes the only local command described by R0-07.
outcomes: Recovery succeeds because R0-20 implies a deployment recovery operation.
The command refuses because a staff account already exists, leaving no specified recovery path.

open_points.subject: snapshot import-result representation
open_points.text: “A producer reads an earlier import result by its `import_id`” and has `portal.estimate_snapshot.read_import_result`
open_points.question: What fields and status states are returned for accepted, idempotent replay, validation rejection, integrity conflict, and processing failure, and when is an `import_id` issued?
options: A closed result schema and status machine covering every terminal result
Only accepted imports receive an `import_id`
Every attempt receives an immutable result, including rejections
open_points.default_guess: Issue an `import_id` for every authenticated import attempt and return an immutable closed result covering accepted, replayed, rejected, conflicted, and failed outcomes.

witness.initial: A producer submits a snapshot with a foreign currency or conflicting fingerprint.
events: The import is rejected.
The producer later reads the result using an import ID.
outcomes: A persisted rejection result is returned with stable reason data.
No import ID/result exists because only accepted imports are retained.
